subject: reasoning
question: A, B, L, M, S, T and Z are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Only four people sit between M and T when counted from the right of M. M sits third to the left of L. S sits third to the left of Z. B is an immediate neighbour of both T and L. How many people sit between A and B when counted from the right of A?
solution:
Given:

A, B, L, M, S, T and Z are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

Only four people sit between M and T when counted from the right of M.

M sits third to the left of L. S sits third to the left of Z.

B is an immediate neighbour of both T and L.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7b0467ec5536f454c1184115fa4bacb66f9232d5fc91d8c9cdb212fd3e404b76.png] 

Thus, 2 people sit between A and B when counted from the right of A.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**
